purpose: Test finite-panel scaling of the fixed two-point CRT curve-choice policy across predetermined prime fields

subgroup_policy.order: largest prime factor of the full base-curve group order
subgroup_policy.generator: multiply the lexicographically first nonidentity base-curve point whose cofactor multiple is nonidentity by the cofactor

target_policy.public_point: scalar times generator, constructed before the target scan
target_policy.admission: both sampled points nonidentity and distinct

curve_choice_policy.point_lifts: center each affine coordinate modulo the base field prime
curve_choice_policy.auxiliary_search_order: increasing sum of centered absolute coefficient residues, then maximum absolute value, then centered lexicographic tuple
curve_choice_policy.crt: each free coefficient is zero mod base prime and is the selected residue mod 7 and 11; center modulo 77p
curve_choice_policy.a4_a6: solve both rational lifted-point equations exactly
curve_choice_policy.acceptance: nonsingular rational curve with good prescribed reductions at base prime, 7, and 11; no alternate order arm

recovery: w=(t1+2t2)/3 mod r for a rational relation, followed by independent scalar replay
raw_rows: deterministic gzip JSONL shards by blocks of eight t1 values; preserve every query and status
first_hit_rule: first accepted rational relation in the frozen lexicographic query order
reference_arm: p=47 must reproduce the earlier fixed-target census and coefficient probe counts
claim_boundary: finite-panel correctness, yield, and candidate-probe counts; no wall-time, asymptotic, or rho comparison
